relations.subject: js-udf:scoped-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - structural evidence: JS UDFs are created/called from the Query tab or by running a SQL++ statement
relations.evidence: You can use user-defined functions (UDFs) to call JavaScript code from the Query Tab.

relations.subject: js-udf:global-function
relations.evidence: If you do not add a prefix before the library name in your SQL++ statement, the user-defined function will be created as a **Global** function. You cannot create another global function called GetBusinessDays on your cluster, but you can create a scoped function called GetBusinessDays.

relations.subject: js-udf:global-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - structural evidence: this page shows SELECT, EXECUTE FUNCTION, and inline-expression calls as three equally-valid ways to invoke the same user-defined function, with no preference stated
relations.evidence: You can also use the EXECUTE FUNCTION statement to execute the function: EXECUTE FUNCTION GetBusinessDays("02/14/2025", "04/16/2025");

notable_absence.finding: Nothing on this page restricts JS UDF creation or invocation to a particular access surface or credential type - UDFs are created 'from the Query tab or by running a SQL++ statement' with no stated exclusion. This page provides no evidence either confirming or denying whether JS UDFs are reachable via the Data API specifically (that evidence comes instead from data-api-use.json's worked SELECT-via-passthrough example and this page's own silence on the topic), but the complete absence of any exclusion language here is itself notable given how explicitly transactions.md and using-ai.md called out their exclusions.

cross_component_finding: This page presents SELECT, EXECUTE FUNCTION, and inline-expression calls as three equally-valid call styles for a side-effect-free UDF with no preference stated - unlike handling-errors-javascript-udf.json and calling-n1ql-from-javascript.json in this same batch, where EXECUTE FUNCTION IS mandatory once the function has side effects (data-changing statements). Recommend the coordinator read this page's silence as the 'no side effects' baseline case, not as contradicting the other two files' stricter requirement.
